items.cite: Macdonald, Hugh. *Bizet*. New York: Oxford University Press, 2014.
items.note: The standard account of how a prize-winning pianist spent his adult life trying to establish himself in the theatre. Use with Macdonald’s online catalogue where a familiar title covers an unfinished project or a later editor’s intervention.

items.cite: McClary, Susan. *Georges Bizet: Carmen*. Cambridge Opera Handbooks. Cambridge: Cambridge University Press, 1992.
items.note: Asks how the opera makes gender, class and its imagined Spain audible, a question the tunes alone cannot answer. Places the score beside Mérimée’s novella, its reception and later adaptations. Especially useful to read before returning to the final duet.

items.cite: Curtiss, Mina. *Bizet and His World*. New York: Alfred A. Knopf, 1958.
items.note: For the people and working conditions behind the operas: letters, family relationships, publishers and Parisian theatres. Its documentary material remains valuable; dates and claims about musical versions should be checked against newer scholarship.

items.cite: Bizet, Georges. *Lettres à un ami, 1865–1872*. Edited by Edmond Galabert. Paris: Calmann-Lévy, 1909.
items.note: For Bizet writing about composition and the practical frustrations of his career before Carmen. The letters were edited and published posthumously; they do not form a diary or an unmediated account of every event.

items.cite: Macdonald, Hugh. *The Bizet Catalogue*. Washington University in St Louis. Online thematic catalogue.
items.note: For checking what Bizet wrote: composition dates, manuscripts, early editions, letters, premières and later alterations. The Carmen and L’Arlésienne entries separate the composer’s work from recitatives, suites and revisions made after his death.
